ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated List, and the Korean government's sanctions list (maintained by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs). Additionally, PEP screening against domestic and international PEP databases, including the World Bank's PEP list and national PEP registers. Enhanced due diligence is required for any match or high-risk jurisdiction. Screening must be conducted at onboarding and on an ongoing basis via automated monitoring systems. All screening results must be documented and retained for at least 5 years, and any suspicious activity must be reported to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) within 24 hours.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Commercial Registration Information System (상업등기정보시스템) operated by the Supreme Court of Korea
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Korean script (Hangul). English names may be used as a secondary name, but must be phonetically transliterated into Hangul. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name. The name must include a legal form indicator such as 'Yuhan Hoesa' (유한회사) for a limited liability company. The name must comply with the four-tier naming convention: (1) unique identifier, (2) business purpose, (3) legal form, and (4) any additional descriptors. Prohibited words require prior ministerial approval.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant may file an objection with the registration court within 14 days of the rejection notice. The court will review the objection and issue a decision within 30 days. If the objection is denied, the applicant may appeal to the higher court within 14 days of the decision. The appeal must include evidence of distinctiveness, compliance with naming rules, and any prior approvals for sensitive tokens. The entire appeal process typically takes 2-4 weeks. During the appeal, the name reservation may be extended by the court upon request.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are generally not permitted for tax registration and bank account opening. The National Tax Service requires a physical address for business registration, and banks require a physical office for verification, especially for foreign-owned entities. A virtual office or commercial mailbox is likely to be rejected by both tax authorities and banks for this industry (ESG consulting). It is strongly recommended to lease a physical office or use a serviced office with a physical presence. A registered agent may be used for service of process, but the registered office must be a physical location in Korea.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: 1. Business registration certificate; 2. Lease agreement; 3. Utility bills; 4. Employee presence; 5. Signage. Risk: Moderate. The National Tax Service and municipal tax office may conduct unannounced physical inspections, especially for newly registered companies. The likelihood is estimated at 20% within the first year of operation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), as supplemented by the Supreme Court Commercial Registration Rules and the Notaries Act. For the Yuhan Hoesa limited liability company, applicable sections include Articles 287-2 through 287-74; incorporation registration is governed by Articles 34, 37, 317 and 318 of the Commercial Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Civil Affairs Department, District Court (Court Registry Office) having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office of the company in the Republic of Korea; online e-filing is available through the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act. However, the full amount of every issued contribution unit must be paid in before the incorporation registration is filed. Monetary contributions must be deposited into a dedicated capital contribution account at a licensed bank, and the bank must not permit withdrawal of those funds until the company is registered and legal personality is conferred. In-kind contributions must be appraised and fully delivered before registration. No blocked escrow account is required, but the capital contribution deposit account is effectively ring-fenced by the bank until the company has been incorporated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Pro-Forma First Board Resolution of KR Yuhang Hoesa. At the registered office of KR Yuhang Hoesa, a Yuhan Hoesa organized under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, the founding members and first directors, duly noticed and waiving formal notice pursuant to the Articles of Incorporation, do hereby unanimously adopt the following resolutions. Resolution Number One: Share Capital Subscription and Contribution. The board ratifies the subscription of every contribution unit shown in the notarized Articles and confirms that each founding member has irrevocably paid the full amount of subscribed capital into the dedicated capital contribution account at a licensed bank. The board orders that the bank certificate of paid-in capital be delivered to the Court Registry Office and that no distribution of capital or withdrawal of contributions be permitted until legal personality is fully registered. Resolution Number Two: Adoption of Registered Office. The board adopts the registered office located at the designated address in the Republic of Korea as the legal seat, mailing address, and service-of-process venue of the company and authorizes the Company Secretary to file the registered office consent and register the office with the National Tax Service. Resolution Number Three: Appointment of Statutory Officers. The board appoints the Chief Executive Officer, the Audit Officer, and the Company Secretary, each to serve until the first annual meeting and until a successor is elected. The Chief Executive Officer and Audit Officer shall have the powers and duties prescribed by the Commercial Act. Resolution Number Four: Banking Authorization. The board opens corporate bank accounts at a licensed commercial bank and appoints banking signatories. Any payment exceeding the authorized threshold requires the joint signature of the Chief Executive Officer and the Company Secretary or the Chief Financial Officer. Resolution Number Five: Regulatory Filing and Contracting Authority. The board authorizes the Chief Executive Officer to execute the business registration application, tax registrations, data protection filings, ESG carbon audit service contracts, offset brokerage agreements, and all lease, procurement, and employment contracts within board-approved limits. Signed, sealed, and delivered this day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Notarize the Articles of Incorporation and Initial Governance Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public authorized under the Notaries Act of the Republic of Korea, or a licensed notary law office in Seoul acting as a lawyer-notary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporating member or its lawful attorney shall prepare definitive Articles of Incorporation for the Yuhan Hoesa in Korean or bilingual format containing the corporate name, purpose including corporate Scope 1-3 carbon footprint auditing, ESG compliance advisory, and carbon offset brokerage, address of the registered office, total capital and contribution units, class and value of each contribution, valuation of in-kind contributions, distribution rules, names of founding members, number and duties of officers, term, accounting period, and dissolution methods. The officer in charge must verify each founding member's identity, execute the articles in person or by notarized power of attorney, and pay the notarial fee. The notary shall certify the due execution and lawful contents of the Articles, thereby producing the original notarized articles required by the Court Registry Office.
required_dossiers: Identity documents and passports of all founding members or legalized power of attorney
Draft Articles of Incorporation signed by all founding members
Registered office reservation consent or lease contract approval
Proof of legal capacity and board approval of the corporate founder, if applicable
Professional business plan or purpose statement for ESG carbon auditing and offset brokerage activity
Certificate of incorporation or business registry abstract of each corporate member, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requires corrections, the incorporator shall execute an amended articles text promptly and pay the additional notarial fee. If identity or authority is questioned, provide a certified power of attorney apostilled or consular-legalized for foreign members, or appear before the same notary in person. If the purpose clause is not specific enough, add an illustrative enumerated list of ESG and carbon-related advisory and brokerage services.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Dedicated Capital Contribution Account and Complete Payment of Issued Contribution Amount
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate banking center or corporate branch of a licensed commercial bank in the Republic of Korea authorized to open capital contribution deposit accounts.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, the company in formation must open a non-withdrawable capital contribution account at a licensed commercial bank; the account must be titled in the name of the proposed Yuhan Hoesa and earmarked as a capital subscription account. Each founding member shall remit from their own account the full amount of subscribed monetary contributions; the bank must verify the identity and beneficial owner of the remitter, confirm the source of funds, and issue a certificate of paid-in capital, namely a deposit certificate or balance certificate, for the registration filing. The funds must remain blocked in the account until the incorporation registration has been completed and the bank receives a certificate of registration. Any in-kind contribution must be delivered and appraised by an approved appraiser or expert before the registration filing, and the appraised value recorded in the notarized Articles.
required_dossiers: Bank application for capital contribution account
Notarized Articles of Incorporation excerpt
Passport and alien registration card of each member or officer
Bank remittance records evidencing source of funds
Written AML/CFT beneficial ownership declaration
Interest and disbursement prohibition letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank withholds the certificate due to anti-money-laundering checks, supply source-of-wealth documents and a beneficial ownership chain. If the deposit is rejected because the remitter is not the registered member, re-route the funds from the member's own verified account. If the asset appraisal is disputed, order a second appraisal under Korean valuation standards or request a court-appointed appraiser before expiry of the registration period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Application for Incorporation Registration with the Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Civil Affairs Department, of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; online submission may be made through the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the paid-in capital certificate is issued, the authorized representative or its legal agent shall prepare and submit the Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa to the competent court registry. The filing must occur within the statutory timeframe from the execution of the Articles. The applicant shall append the notarized Articles, paid-in capital certificate, consent to use the registered office by the lessor, member register, appointment and acceptance forms of officers, and a copy of each officer's identity. The registry officer will examine compliance with the Commercial Act, verify payment of registration tax and education surtax, check the capital deposit certificate and no-withdrawal condition, and, if satisfied, issue a corporate registration certificate and register the company in the commercial register. Electronic filing users must attach scanned originals and pay fees through the approved portal.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of paid-in contribution deposit issued by the bank
Application for Registration of Incorporation
Consent of the owner of the registered office or lease agreement
Register of members and officers
Officer appointment and acceptance declarations
Corporate seal specimen card
Proof of payment of registration taxes and court fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a written supplementation order, cure precisely within the stated period by submitting missing certified copies or consents. Failure to cure timely may allow the registrar to reject, in which case the applicant may apply for correction or appeal through an objection under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act. Where the portal rejects scanned documents, file in paper at the court counter or ask a local legal agent to facilitate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Business Registration with the National Tax Service and Municipal Start-Up Reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service through the Home Tax Service online portal or the district tax office of the registered office; local municipal government for business start-up and corporate seal registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within approximately one month after the court registration, the company must apply for a corporate business registration certificate by filing the corporate business registration application with the National Tax Service. The application is made online at Home Tax or in person at the district tax office. The company must also register for value-added tax, corporate income tax, withheld payroll taxes, and electronic invoice issuance. As part of the same step, the company must register its corporate seal with the competent municipal office in order to obtain an official seal certificate. No separate operating license is required for pure digital ESG advisory and carbon accounting services. The returned business registration certificate, assigned tax identification number, and seal certificate shall be entered into the corporate books.
required_dossiers: Corporate registration certificate from the Court Registry Office
Certificate of corporate seal registration
Business registration application form
Articles of Incorporation notarized copy
Lease agreement or registered office ownership evidence
Officer identity and appointment documents
Bank account proof if available
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service returns the application due to missing tax classification or address issues, file a corrected application through Home Tax. If the municipal office delays seal certification, re-apply after obtaining the court registration summary and a notarized seal card. Any material error in tax classification must be corrected by filing an amendment before tax invoice cycles commence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Final Corporate Governance Resolutions, Open Operating Bank Accounts, and Issue Legal Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors or founding officer acting under the Articles and First Board Resolution; corporate banking department of the chosen commercial bank; municipal seal certificate office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Board shall formally adopt the First Board Resolution confirming issuance and payment of capital, registered office, banking signatories, statutory officer appointments, and delegations. A certified copy of the resolution shall be inserted in the statutory minute book and served on the bank and tax representative. The company shall open a current operating bank account and a separate escrow or settlement account for carbon offset brokerage funds if applicable, supplying the court registration certificate, corporate seal certificate, passports of officers, and the Board Resolution. The company shall also execute the corporate seal registration, sign a service-level agreement with an external audit firm, and issue internal compliance policies for data protection and ESG reporting. All books must be kept at the registered office.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution executed and minuted
Certified copy of the corporate registration certificate
Corporate seal registration certificate
Corporate bank account opening forms and authorized signatory cards
Passport or ID and resident proof of the board members
Original Articles of Incorporation
AML/CFT beneficial ownership disclosure of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank imposes enhanced due diligence for a foreign-owned consulting company, submit certified copies of registering documents together with an apostilled board resolution and a notarized shareholding schedule. If the seal certificate is lost during opening, request a re-issuance from the municipal office and file a lost-seal report. If a board member is unavailable, a valid alternate director may execute under a power of attorney annexed to the minutes.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. The entity will not maintain a manufacturing plant, chemical facility, assembly line, or warehouse anywhere in South Korea. The business is a professional ESG carbon auditing and advisory service under ISIC 7020 and NAICS 541620.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. No separate manufacturing or industrial operating permit is required for corporate Scope 1-3 carbon footprint auditing, ESG compliance advice, or carbon offset brokerage carried out as digital and professional consulting services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt. No physical project or facility triggering an Environmental Impact Assessment under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act of the Republic of Korea is proposed; a professional office lease does not require an environmental assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. The business will generate zero industrial wastewater, zero point-source air emissions, and no hazardous waste from production activities. If a standard office lease is executed, general municipal waste disposal through the building manager will comply with the Waste Control Act and applicable municipal ordinances.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable. No fire-safety-certifiable industrial plant is required. However, the leased professional office must comply with building fire safety and emergency evacuation requirements under the Fire-Fighting Facility Installation, Maintenance and Safety Management Act, verified by the building operator's fire certificate. Occupational safety obligations under the Occupational Safety and Health Act administered by the Ministry of Employment and Labor apply only to ordinary office workplace safety and emergency plans.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, operating through the HomeTax electronic tax portal; for export clearance and customs-related substantiation, Korea Customs Service (KCS) through the UNI-PASS electronic clearance portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident shareholder forming a Yuhan Hoesa must appoint a Korean tax representative and establish a domestic place of business. The representative must prepare an apostilled or consular-legalized certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, certificate of good standing, board resolution approving the Korean establishment, passport copies, power of attorney for the Korean representative, local office lease, and evidence of the registered business address. The application is filed with the National Tax Service district tax office as a foreign corporation business registration application via HomeTax or in-person submission. NTS verifies the Korean business place and issues the Business Registration Certificate (Business Registration Number), which serves as the entity TIN and VAT registration number. If the entity intends to export, it must also register as an importer/exporter in the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system to obtain a customs registration number. The entity must then activate a HomeTax e-tax invoice account, obtain and install the NTS-issued digital certificate, and appoint a corporate accounting officer for VAT compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea does not provide US-style check-the-box or entity classification elections. A Yuhan Hoesa is a domestic corporation by law and is mandatorily subject to entity-level corporate income tax under the Corporate Tax Act. The only elective mechanism remotely relevant is the statutory Korean tax consolidation regime for a qualifying domestic corporate group; no hybrid mismatch or entity-disregard election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0 - no statutory economic turnover threshold; every business that supplies taxable goods or services in the Republic of Korea must register with the National Tax Service before commencing business, regardless of revenue. A Korean LLC is a general taxable corporate VAT person and is not eligible for the simplified small-business VAT regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoicing through the National Tax Service HomeTax e-tax invoice system or an approved service provider. The Korean LLC must issue an electronic VAT invoice for each taxable B2B supply, include the NTS-validated business registration number, transmit the invoice data to NTS, and retain the standard XML retention copy. Korea does not operate a per-transaction real-time clearance block chain or fiscal stamping machine; integrity control is achieved through NTS electronic validation, encrypted authentication certificates, periodic transmission obligations, and cross-matching against customs and bank settlement data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated status is available on the export of goods physically removed from Korea, on supplies of services performed for non-residents where the service is used outside Korea, and on qualifying offshore digital services. For ESG carbon accounting and offset advisory exports, the Korean LLC must establish that the recipient is a non-resident enterprise, the carbon audit and advisory deliverable is performed for and consumed at the foreign client site, the contract is denominated in a foreign currency, and consideration is received offshore. If any part of the service is consumed by a Korean domestic fixed establishment or relates to Korean-located assets, that part is subject to VAT at 10%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS export clearance declaration (Export Customs Declaration) evidencing export from the Republic of Korea
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing physical movement of goods to the foreign destination

Foreign exchange settlement confirmation / Inward Remittance Certificate (or equivalent bank transaction report issued under the Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act) proving receipt of export consideration in foreign currency from the overseas buyer
Export contract, purchase order, and title transfer evidence showing the non-resident buyer accepted the goods or services

For intangible ESG/carbon advisory services: signed service agreement, documented scope of work, electronically delivered carbon audit report or carbon credit brokerage confirmation, and foreign recipient acceptance evidence demonstrating offshore consumption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: A zero-rated export claim that lacks credible customs, shipping, or foreign-exchange repatriation evidence is recharacterized as a domestic taxable supply, and NTS will assess VAT at 10% on the full consideration. Previously refunded input VAT, including VAT refunds claimed on export-purchases, is subject to retrospective clawback with statutory interest and additional tax penalties. Fraudulent or falsely documented zero-rating, including inflated export invoices or false e-tax invoices, is subject to criminal prosecution under Korean tax penalty law, imprisonment, fines, and denial or suspension of export VAT refunds; repeated or aggravated cases may attract penalty surcharges calculated as a percentage of the false supply value plus collection proceedings under the National Tax Collection Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), exercising powers under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA) and Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations; the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) retains policy rule-making authority for capital transaction liberalization and foreign exchange administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates an export-driven, regulated liberal current account and a partially liberalized capital account. The Korean won is convertible for documented current transactions such as trade settlements, service fees, and direct investment, but all cross-border transactions must be routed through a licensed foreign exchange bank and reported in the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS). Current account convertibility is effectively full once the bank verifies the underlying contract, invoice, customs declaration, or tax invoice; funds are credited to a resident foreign currency account. Capital account convertibility, including equity injection into a Korean LLC, debt financing, or acquisition of foreign assets, is permissible but requires a foreign exchange declaration and, for foreign investment of KRW 100 million or above, registration under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA). Profit remittance by way of dividends is freely convertible upon presentation of audited financial statements, board appropriation resolution, withholding tax calculation, and tax receipt; the remitting bank will not process dividends until the withholding tax has been paid. Excess funds in KRW may be converted to foreign currency only with a documented reason, and the bank must submit the transaction to FEIS. No broad capital flow localization or surrender ringfence exists for ordinary profits, but a treasury must maintain documentary integrity because the penalty for misclassified capital flows is heavy and can freeze the entity's banking access.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under FETA and the Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, export proceeds must be received in foreign currency through a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank generally within 18 months from the date of export declaration; an extension may be granted only by the Bank of Korea or the competent foreign exchange bank for justifiable commercial, judicial, or force majeure reasons. Once received, the proceeds may be credited to a resident foreign currency deposit account, and the mandatory conversion ratio to KRW is 0%; exporters are not obliged to surrender export proceeds. However, any conversion to Korean won must be executed at market rates through a licensed bank, and the receipt and any subsequent FX conversion must be reported in FEIS to maintain the audit trail.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and USD)
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Very Low. Offshore digital EMIs and non-bank e-money institutions are legally barred from acting as the primary treasury rail for a South Korean resident corporation, because FETA requires foreign exchange and cross-border payment business to be conducted only by banks licensed as foreign exchange banks in Korea. Offshore EMIs cannot issue a resident Korean account, cannot access the Korean Won clearing infrastructure, and cannot make FEIS reports. An overseas EMI may be used only as a non-settlement ancillary invoicing/API layer, while all actual fund movement and FX conversion must remain in a Tier-1 licensed Korean bank; attempting to use an EMI for KRW settlement creates material risk of unlicensed money transmission and account termination.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical branch appearance is not an absolute statutory mandate under the Real-Name Financial Transaction Act, but it is the de facto majority requirement among Tier-1 Korean banks for the initial corporate account activation of a non-resident-owned Yuhan Hoesa. Most compliance committees require at least one statutory director or UBO with a notarized, apostilled directorship certificate to appear at a domestic Korea branch for an in-person KYC interview. Where the director is outside Korea, remote video KYC plus a local Korean resident representative appointed by a notarized and apostilled power of attorney may be acceptable on a risk-override basis, but pure consular proxy opening without any video interview is generally rejected.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque or multi-layered non-resident UBO chain with controlling interests held through offshore holding entities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified and notarized corporate organization chart; register of members and shareholders showing all legal and natural persons owning 25% or more or exercising de facto control; certificate of incumbency for each offshore entity; passport copies with notarization/apostille; consolidated or audited financial statements of the ultimate parent for the last two years; and a legal opinion confirming tax residence in a FATF-compliant jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Carbon offset brokerage activity can be misread as an unlicensed settlement or money transmission service if revenues merely pass through the entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed carbon advisory and brokerage agreements; Verra, Gold Standard, or Korea KETS registry statements showing the carbon credits; escrow and custodial account agreements; itemized invoices for advisory fees and commission; a written opinion from a Korean licensed accountant that the fee structure is commission/advisory and not customer money transmission; and the entity's internal AML/CFT policies and procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital contribution from a foreign shareholder with incomplete source-of-wealth and capital account reporting.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A capital transaction report or foreign investment declaration accepted by a licensed foreign exchange bank under FETA/FIPA; board resolution authorizing the equity injection; source-of-wealth evidence including three months of personal/business bank statements, income tax returns, audited financial statements, and sale or loan agreements supporting the remittance; and a certified copy of the receipt of foreign funds from the bank for capital verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, adverse media, or cross-border counterparty exposure arising from carbon projects connected to a sanctioned jurisdiction or high-risk jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions, PEP, and adverse media screening reports for shareholders, directors, all counterparties, and the underlying project sites; compliance declarations from every carbon registry showing no origination in or sale to UN/OFAC/EU/UK/Democratic People's Republic of Korea sanctioned territories; detailed commercial contract files and chain-of-custody documents; and bank-approved escrow or restricted account language for any project with a medium-risk geography.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital must be wired in foreign currency by SWIFT MT103 to the entity's capital escrow or designated operational account at a licensed Tier-1 Korean bank. The remitter must include the Korean foreign investment declaration number or foreign exchange bank capital transaction reference, and the remittance purpose must be tagged as paid-in capital / FDI equity injection. The beneficiary bank will verify the foreign investment report, credit the funds to the escrow account, and submit the receipt to FEIS. For any foreign investment over KRW 100 million, the company must first file a foreign investment report under FIPA and open the capital account in the same bank. The escrow balance may not be spent on operating expenses until the required capital verification has been issued by a licensed Korean certified public accountant or external auditor, unless the bank's policy permits an early-use waiver after FEIS confirmation. All conversion of the inbound foreign currency to KRW must be executed at market rate by the foreign exchange bank with a documented purpose code.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For service-type disbursements under ISIC 7020 ESG carbon advisory activities, the primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 from the entity's Korean account to the counterparty's bank, with the payment memo referencing the invoice and underlying services agreement. If the payment relates to importation of stationary or commodity-linked carbon credits, a Commercial Letter of Credit or Documentary Collection can be opened through the same bank with presentation of commercial invoice, bill of lading or air waybill, insurance documents, and the carbon registry transfer statement. The bank will debit the KRW account, convert at market FX rate, and report the service or capital transaction purpose in FEIS. Before execution the bank will require a full settlement-support package including contract, invoice, proof of delivery or performance, and tax invoice for VAT if applicable; failure to submit underlying documents will block disbursement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable forward foreign exchange contracts in USD/KRW and major currency pairs, permitted only when the Yuhan Hoesa can evidence an underlying trade, service contract, or capital transaction that creates genuine FX exposure.

FX swaps and cross-currency interest rate swaps for hedging foreign-currency loans or long-term ESG project investments, provided the instruments are executed with a licensed foreign exchange bank, reported through FEIS, and approved by the board.
Purchased currency options with real-demand support, while writing or selling options by a non-bank corporate is treated as speculative and is not permitted.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not a recommended onshore corporate instrument for Korean residents; their use is materially restricted, and treasury operations should rely on deliverable forwards and swaps with documented real demand to avoid regulatory recharacterization.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return with tax adjustment schedules and approved financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) - jurisdictional district tax office through Home Tax Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 following a December 31 fiscal year-end; if a different fiscal year is adopted, within three months from the close of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late or omitted corporate tax return attracts an unfiled-return surtax generally equal to 20 percent of the tax payable, or 40 percent for fraudulent omission, plus daily overdue interest of approximately 0.022 percent on unpaid corporate tax. The NTS may issue a demand, seize bank accounts and receivables, deny tax clearance certificates, and, after prolonged delinquency and business dormancy, issue a business closure notification. Korea does not provide an automatic registry strike-off for a delinquent annual filing, but creditors or members may petition the court for judicial dissolution if the company is inactive and persistently non-compliant.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax Return and payment of the local surtax on corporate income tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government revenue office with jurisdiction over the registered office (Si/Gun/Gu or Provincial revenue department)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the corporate income tax deadline; for a calendar-year entity, no later than March 31 following the close of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment or underdeclaration triggers an additional local tax of up to 10 percent of the deficient local tax amount, daily late-payment interest at the locally prescribed per-day rate, and coercive collection through local government seizure. Chronic delinquency may lead to tax lien enforcement, business closure notification, and eventual court dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Members Annual General Meeting, approval of financial statements, and appointment or re-election of the corporate auditor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate organ internal process; resolutions recorded in the statutory minute book; no court filing unless a registered corporate fact changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of each fiscal year; a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa must hold the meeting no later than March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene carries no direct government filing fee, but the financial statements are not legally deemed approved. Persistent failure to hold member meetings may be used by the NTS to treat the company as non-transparent, may support creditors seeking judicial dissolution, and may prevent the company from satisfying the formalities required for credit or licensing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial Statements and External Auditor Report filing for a company subject to mandatory statutory audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART electronic disclosure system; a copy of the audited financial statements is attached to the NTS corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end, by April 30 following the fiscal year-end or within three weeks after completion of the external audit if the audit report is finalized after the annual general meeting; in no event later than the statutory tax return deadline where the NTS requires audited statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain or file a mandatory external audit report is punishable by administrative fines under the Korean External Audit Act, with maximum fines around KRW 50 million. The unaudited financial statements are inadmissible for statutory purposes, the NTS may recompute taxable income using estimated assessments, and continued non-compliance may trigger enhanced tax collection actions, business closure, and judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Enterprise Annual Report and renewal of foreign-investment filing status where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through KOTRA or the delegated foreign investment administrative authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the last business day of February following the close of each fiscal year if the Yuhan Hoesa has non-resident Korean direct investment subject to notification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing may attract an administrative fine not exceeding KRW 5 million and may result in forfeiture of foreign-investment tax incentives, delay of foreign exchange clearance, and adverse marking of the foreign investment registration status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of ultimate beneficial ownership and maintenance of the statutory member register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service as an annex or schedule to the corporate income tax return; Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) reporting where an AML-triggering transaction occurs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation on or before March 31 with the corporate income tax return; within 30 days after any material shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate, incomplete, or fraudulent beneficial ownership information may attract tax report penalties and AML-related administrative sanctions; failure to maintain the member register at the registered office is a statutory record-keeping violation that may be treated as a corporate register default, exposing the company to non-criminal fines and making it ineligible for certain clearances.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, Etc., a Yuhan Hoesa LLC is subject to mandatory independent certified CPA audit if its total assets at the immediately preceding fiscal year-end are at least KRW 12 billion, approximately USD 9.2 million at 1,300 KRW/USD. The entity is also audited if it is a public-interest entity, financial company, or special industry requiring a CPA certification. There is no statutory turnover or headcount test for a private Yuhan Hoesa; the controlling quantitative bright-line trigger is the balance-sheet total asset threshold of KRW 12 billion. If total assets are below this threshold, an audit becomes mandatory only in special circumstances such as shareholder request or supervisory requirement, not through ordinary annual filing.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared under Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) if the Yuhan Hoesa is listed, financial, or designated as a public-interest entity. A non-listed private Yuhan Hoesa may apply Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP or Accounting Standards for Non-Listed Entities) consistently. The chosen framework must comply with the Korean Accounting Standards Board requirements and present a true and fair view; for companies above the statutory audit threshold, audited financial statements under either K-IFRS or K-GAAP are accepted only when accompanied by an independent certified audit report.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not operate a standalone annual UBO certificate for a private limited liability company, but the Yuhan Hoesa must confirm ultimate beneficial ownership through the annual corporate income tax filing and must maintain the statutory member register at its registered office. Any transfer of a member equity interest requires a member meeting resolution unless the articles of incorporation provide otherwise, and the transfer becomes enforceable against the company only after the member register is updated. Shareholding changes triggering a change in capital, registered directors, or other registered corporate facts must be filed with the Commercial Registration Office within 14 days. Where a shareholding transfer changes beneficial ownership and the company is engaged in an AML-reportable financial transaction through a Korean financial institution, the 30-day reporting window under the Specific Financial Transaction Information Act is applied. Tax authorities may require updated ultimate shareholder information to be reflected on the annual tax return; thus the practical annual protocol is a March 31 UBO confirmation filing with the NTS and a 30-day event-driven ownership change notice.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 22,000 per year depending on transaction volume, asset size, and carbon accounting scope complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top marginal (progressive: 9% up to KRW 200m; 19% over KRW 200m; 21% over KRW 20bn; 24% over KRW 300bn)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for a Seoul-headquartered ESG/carbon audit LLC; available incentives include a 15-20% R&D tax credit for certified carbon-accounting software development, a 5% green facility investment tax credit, and an income deduction of up to 10% for clean-energy asset investment; free-zone preferential regimes do not apply because business is in the general unitary Korean tax jurisdiction.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Final Return (the primary Korean NTS return form) filed electronically through HomeTax, the National Tax Service e-filing portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the end of the financial year; for a 31 December year-end, the filing deadline is 31 March; a domestic LLC that is wholly or partially foreign-owned is not generally entitled to an extended four-month time limit unless a legal disability or court-appointed tax agent applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income, cost of sales, and deductible operating expenses used to compute adjusted taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all worldwide income, including cross-border ESG audit fees and carbon brokerage commissions; any payment from a foreign parent for head-office services must be supported by written agreements and actual service evidence; foreign-exchange gains on client wire transfers are taxable Korean-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax base reconciliation line adding tax-exempt income, permanent establishment profit attribution, and loss carryforward set-off.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source dividend and carbon-offset brokerage income is included before treaty relief; carryforward losses must be deducted in statutory order, and non-resident shareholders must not claim tax-exempt status for Korean domestic activities simply because the entity is foreign-owned.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tentative corporate tax, derived by applying the progressive rate schedule to the tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute at the 9-19-21-24% progressive brackets; attach full computation if the non-resident parent's recharged expenses were adjusted by the tax authority; remember that national corporate tax computed here is the basis for the 10% local income tax surcharge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit schedule and deduction for overseas withholding taxes on carbon-offset brokerage income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply credit only for taxes paid on foreign-source income that is included in the Korean tax base; use the per-country limitation formula; directly related foreign taxes on carbon-credit purchase intermediaries must be evidenced by official foreign tax receipts to avoid double taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party cross-border transaction schedule covering intercompany services, royalties, interest, and capital financing, together with a non-resident participation declaration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare all transactions with foreign related parties, including carbon-credit brokerage fees paid to an overseas ESG affiliate; attach transfer pricing documents when the statutory threshold is exceeded; unrecognized cross-border service fees may be denied as deductions and treated as constructive dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax reconciliation for outbound dividend, interest, and royalty payments and proof of treaty relief claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withhold at the 16.5% statutory domestic rate before remittance unless a tax treaty reduction is approved; attach the foreign owner's Tax Residence Certificate, beneficial ownership statement, and the HomeTax treaty relief application; untreated omitted withholding exposes the Korean LLC to collection liability and penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: If the return is not filed, NTS imposes an additional tax equal to 10% of the unpaid corporate tax; negligent underreporting attracts a 20% surcharge and fraudulent underreporting attracts a 40% surcharge; late payment also accrues daily late-payment interest on the unpaid national tax and the 10% local income tax surcharge; criminal tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act can result in imprisonment up to five years and fines up to twice the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 16.5% (15% corporate income tax withholding plus 1.5% local income tax surcharge); a bilateral tax treaty may reduce the rate to 10% or 5% depending on shareholding and beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must obtain a valid Tax Residence Certificate from its residence country, complete and submit through HomeTax the Application for Tax Treaty Exemption/Reduction of Withholding, provide a signed beneficial ownership statement, and the Korean payer must file the application with the district tax office before remittance; if treaty relief is claimed only after tax was withheld, a refund must be claimed within five years; the Korean general anti-avoidance rule and limitation-on-benefits provisions deny relief where the ultimate beneficiary lacks substance or is a conduit.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding is 16.5% (15% national plus 1.5% local surcharge) for both royalties and interest; most Korean bilateral treaties set interest at 10% and royalties at 10%, with some treaties providing 5% for dividends paid to substantial shareholders and 5% for certain industrial royalties; treaty reduction is available only when the recipient presents a Tax Residence Certificate and demonstrates actual beneficial ownership of the income.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory when total annual revenue equals or exceeds KRW 10 billion and cross-border related-party transactions equal or exceed KRW 5 billion; Master File is required when cross-border related-party transactions equal or exceed KRW 10 billion and total revenue equals or exceeds KRW 100 billion; Country-by-Country Report is due for multinational groups with consolidated revenue above KRW 1 trillion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea has no separate free-zone ESR filing, but substance is enforced through the substance-over-form rule under Corporate Tax Act Article 14, the real-transactions doctrine, the OECD transfer pricing framework, and treaty limitation-on-benefits / principal-purpose-test safeguards; a Yuhan Hoesa must maintain local office, payroll, director decision-making, risk control, and core income-generating activities in Korea to avoid profit re-attribution and denial of treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording carbon-offset brokerage revenue as non-taxable or booking fabricated offset credits and audit expenses through a non-resident shell intermediary, coupled with intentional omission from the corporate income tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fraudulent tax evasion is subject to the Korean Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3(1): imprisonment for up to five years or a fine of up to twice the evaded corporate tax; NTS additionally imposes the 40% fraudulent underreporting surcharge and daily late-payment interest, and the corporate tax return can be recomputed without any deduction for sham carbon-credit invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The NTS can pierce the Yuhan Hoesa corporate veil where the director controlled the sham intermediary; responsible officers are jointly and severally liable for corporate tax and penalties, may be subject to civil asset restitution, travel bans and tax blacklisting, and face criminal imprisonment up to five years, with seizure of overseas bank accounts and carbon-offset proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing consulting and royalty fees to a foreign related party that performs no core income-generating activity while the Korean carbon audit team performs all substantive work, thereby shifting taxable profit offshore and understating Korean corporate tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The International Tax Adjustment Act Articles 4 and 6 permit NTS to adjust the intercompany price to an arm's length result; the adjustment attracts a 20% negligence penalty or 40% fraudulent understatement penalty, daily late-payment interest, and denial of the deduction for undocumented intercompany service charges; failure to file transfer pricing disclosure forms triggers separate non-compliance penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or organize the false invoices can be held personally liable for the adjusted tax and penalties, subjected to overseas travel blacklisting, and prosecuted for tax evasion; where the corporation is insolvent after the adjustment, directors must make civil restitution from personal assets and may receive imprisonment up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Beneficial Ownership Compliance Failure in Cross-Border Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting wire payments from foreign ESG funds and settling carbon-credit purchases to a third-country special purpose vehicle without performing standard customer due diligence, identifying the ultimate beneficial owner, or filing a suspicious transaction report as required for cross-border payment intermediation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Information Act and the Act on Prevention of Money Laundering impose criminal penalties of up to three years imprisonment or KRW 30 million fines for willful failure to identify beneficial owners or to report suspicious transactions; NTS and the Financial Intelligence Unit may blacklist the entity and impose administrative fines and registration cancellation penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: For willful AML avoidance, the corporate veil is pierced and directors face personal civil liability for the amounts involved, travel bans and financial blacklisting, up to three years criminal imprisonment, and confiscation of the suspicious wire proceeds.
